propositions: Changing a ticket's type silently carries forward a plan-review verdict computed under different criteria, because the reuse functions compare only material fingerprint and code SHA, never the ticket type.

Type gates scoring in four places in the orchestrator and workflow, so a plan passing under one type (e.g., bug with exemptions) may fail under another (e.g., task without exemptions), but stored attestations do not account for this.

The reuse paths in reuse.py (idempotent_reuse and verdict_reuse) do not compare stored ticket_type against the current context type before replaying a verdict, allowing an incorrect verdict to persist after retype.
The REVIEW_RESULT sidecar already records ticket_type, so no schema change is required; only the reuse predicates must read and compare it.

Both reuse paths must fail open—returning None to trigger a full re-review—only when stored and current types are both truthy and differ; sidecars with absent or empty type continue to reuse to avoid mass invalidation.

After retype from bug to task with the fix applied, review-plan runs a full re-review (runner is not reused) rather than replaying the bug-verdict, validating that the same plan can produce different verdicts under different types.
